author: Tim
title: Girl Pulled From Class For Wearing Union Flag Dress
text:
A 12-year-old girl was pulled out of class and put in isolation for wearing a Union flag dress on her school’s culture day. She had written a speech about British history and tradition, but the school told her the dress was “unacceptable”.
Courtney Wright, a straight-A student, was left sitting in the reception until her dad came to get her. She was embarrassed and confused, not understanding what she did wrong.
Her dad, Stuart Field, said: “Courtney was so embarrassed and couldn’t understand what she’d done wrong. She should not be made to feel embarrassed about being British.”
He said the school promoted the event as inclusive, but then rejected her dress and didn’t even listen to the speech she prepared. Other students wearing St George’s and Welsh flags were turned away too.
One student wearing a flat cap and checked shirt was also told to leave. Stuart said: “It just seemed anything that was remotely British wasn’t allowed.”
He added: “Somebody at the school has politicised a Union Jack dress even though that was clearly not Courtney’s intent. Courtney didn’t do anything to be political.”
Courtney had chosen the outfit and written her speech on her own. Stuart said: “She’s a straight A student, one of the brightest in her year and she’s never been in trouble before so she was really upset.”
He asked for answers, but staff gave him the runaround. He was told he’d get a call but didn’t, so he took Courtney out to eat to make her feel better.
He said: “If anything I was extremely proud of what she chosen and what she had written in her speech.”
The school later apologized, which Stuart believes only happened because the governors got involved. But he said: “The damage had already been done, Courtney should not be have been made to feel that way.”
The school now wants her to come back and read the speech, but she doesn’t feel comfortable anymore. Stuart said she feels like they’re parading her now.
Her speech included: “Today I want to talk about my culture — British culture — and why it’s important to me.” It went on to talk about tea, the royal family, Shakespeare, and fish and chips.
She also wrote: “Being British is still a culture, and it matters too. It’s part of who I am. So let’s celebrate all cultures — whether they come from far away or right here at home.”
